speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help your newborn, could you tell me when the breathing trouble started and if you noticed any blue color around the lips? Also, was the baby born prematurely or at full term?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Was the amniotic fluid clear, or did it appear meconium-stained? Also, did you notice any grunting or nasal flaring in the baby immediately after birth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the medical team perform a chest X-ray or a blood gas analysis yet to assess the lung status and oxygenation levels? Please let me know the results if available.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth at 33 weeks of gestation. Social history: N/A

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest Radiograph: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs; Arterial Blood Gas: pH 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2 50 mmHg (elevated), PaO2 60 mmHg (reduced), HCO3- 24 mEq/L.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the prematurity, symptoms, and the classic ground-glass appearance on the X-ray, I have enough information to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (Hyaline Membrane Disease).
